title: Deterministic decision from a universal simulator
statement: Let $c$ be an effective code for nondeterministic Boolean machines, and suppose there is a finite-state nondeterministic Boolean machine $U_N$ such that for every Boolean string $\alpha$ there is a natural number $C$ for which, on every Boolean input $x$ and time bound $t$, every choice sequence of length exactly $C(t+1)$ makes $U_N$ halt on $\langle\langle\mathrm{bits}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$. Suppose also that $U_N$ has an accepting computation of exactly that length if and only if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ has an accepting computation on $x$ using exactly $t$ choices. Then there is a finite-state deterministic Boolean machine $B_F$ such that, for each $\alpha$, some natural number $C$ works for every $x$ and $t$: if the decoded machine accepts $x$ using exactly $t$ choices, $B_F$ computes output $[1]$ on the paired input at exactly $C2^{C(t+1)}$ steps; if it does not, $B_F$ computes output $[0]$ on that input at exactly the same time.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is an effective code for nondeterministic Boolean machines with two work tapes

replaced:
Let $c$ be an effective code for a nondeterministic machine, and suppose there is a
finite nondeterministic Turing machine $U_N$ such that for every code word $\alpha$
there is a natural number $C$ with the following property. For every binary input $x$
and time bound $t$, $U_N$ halts on the encoding of $(t,\alpha,x)$ within $C(t+1)$ steps,
and it accepts that input within that many steps if and only if the machine decoded from
$\alpha$ accepts $x$ within $t$ steps. Then there is a finite deterministic Turing
machine $B_F$ such that for every $\alpha$ there is a natural number $C$ for which, for
every $x$ and $t$, if the decoded machine accepts $x$ within $t$ steps, then $B_F$
computes the one-symbol output $[1]$ on the encoding of $(t,\alpha,x)$ within
$C\,2^{C(t+1)}$ steps; if it does not accept within $t$ steps, then $B_F$ computes $[0]$
on that encoded input within the same bound.
